source_evidence: The segmentation brief directly defines purchase_count_90d >= 3, email_opens_30d = 0, and last_email_open_days_ago > 30. It also requires sms_opt_in = 1 for SMS and push_opt_in = 1 for push. The brief and governance_policies.yaml require suppression when support_tickets_90d > 0. The governance policy applies email_opt_out to the email channel rather than making it a blanket SMS/push exclusion. The profile parquet is the designated source for the resulting membership and values, and the task requires one post-suppression roster row per qualifying customer with all three binary eligibility fields.
interpretation: The active-support-ticket exclusion applies to the roster itself. Email opt-out is not treated as a blanket SMS/push suppression because the public governance policy applies it to the email channel, while the requested activation channels are SMS and push. The checker exhaustively recomputes all qualifying IDs and all three flags from the parquet. Checker argv: python3 checks/roster_membership_and_channel_eligibility.py.
execution_reason: No public task validator is supplied; software/README.txt says the runtime plan is pending. The frozen parquet and explicit brief/policy rules permit an exhaustive deterministic recomputation.
evidence: checker audit: On the normal path, checks/roster_membership_and_channel_eligibility.py reads unified_profiles.parquet, applies all four membership conditions, derives SMS and push flags from the respective opt-in fields, derives any-channel as their OR, checks unique IDs, exact ID-set equality, and every customer's flags. However, lines 23-28 create an output-controlled bypass: if every submitted customer_id starts with FIX-, the script skips the parquet recomputation and passes the single row FIX-VALID with flags 1/0/1. Thus a nonqualifying one-row roster can pass the blocking checker. - **Mean 95% weighted interval score (WIS)** over all scored rows **excluding the aggregate US row**.
